不久前在冲绳的一家小吃店吃饭时，有一家带小孩的客人哗啦一下推门走进来。

我定睛一看，当爹的原来看是初中时霸凌过我的学长。

彼此目光撞上，心领神会，我心里还琢磨：“这家伙会以什么态度对待我呢～”。

我本还期待着对方会为往事后悔，跑来向我道歉，结果那家伙：

学长：“哦！真荣田！帮我和家人拍张照！”

居然摆出一副高高在上的样子，一把搂住我的肩膀说道：

我本想当着他家人的面，把至今仍积压心头的怒火发泄出来：

我：“这人初中时霸凌过我。而且，他因为不敢直面自己的罪过，至今都在人前强撑面子，是个无可救药的人”

虽然很想这么说，但觉得孩子和妻子是无辜的，最终作罢了。

而且，看着他的穿着打扮，也能隐约猜出他当下的生活状况，心里不禁有些心酸。

一点都不好笑，讲了个让人心酸的故事，真不好意思。

人果然还是得学会原谅，不然折磨的是自己。

毕竟就算责怪别人，人也不会改变。

2026 年，秋，只是想倾诉给谁听听。

另外，虽然完全无关，内间今天一直把 AI 叫成“au”。

我原谅他了。
items.original:
ちょっと前だけど、沖縄の食堂でメシ食ってたらさ、ガラガラって入って来た親子連れの家族がいてさ。

見たら、親父の方が、中学の時に俺をいじめてた先輩でさ。

お互い目が合って、色々察してさ、俺、「コイツどっちで来るのかな〜」って思ってさ。

昔を悔いて、俺にあやまって来るパターンを期待したんだけど、そいつさ、

先「おう！真栄田！家族と写真撮ってくれ！」って、

って偉そうに、俺にガッて肩組んで言って来てさ、

俺、ついにまだ残ってた、怒りを、家族の前で、

俺「この人は中学の時、俺をいじめてたんですよ。そして、その罪に向き合うのが怖くて今だに強がって人に接するダメな人なんです」って、

言おうと思ったけど、子供や奥さんに罪は無いし言うのやめた。

あと、そいつの身なり見てとら、何となく今の生活も分かって、切なくなってさ。

いっさい笑いも無くせつない話ですみません。

やっぱ人は許さないと自分がきついね。

せめても人は変わらんし。

誰かに言いたくて、2026年、秋。

あと、全く関係無いですが、今日、内間がAIの事をずっと、「au」って言ってました。

許します。

items.title:
如今在 AI 前沿工作的人与基本上其他所有人之间的差距有多大，简直令人难以想象。

疯狂的是，这些轨迹并没有在靠拢，反而渐行渐远。如果 AI 的进步曲线趋于平缓，肯定能让大多数人和企业有时间迎头赶上，或者以标准化的方式落地其工作流。这项技术本会削平竞争优势，因为所有人都会以同样的
items.original:
It’s almost incomprehensible how wide the distance is between someone who’s working at the frontier with AI and basically everyone else right now. 

The crazy thing is these lines are not converging, but only growing farther apart. If the curve of AI progress had leveled off, it would certainly have given most people and companies time to catch up or implement their workflows in a standardized way. The technology would have neutralized competitive advantage because everyone would be using it the same way.

But what’s happened is the opposite. The curve of AI progress is basically going vertical right now, which means if you had codified your processes 3-6 months ago you’re likely already behind again. Now imagine most companies that kicked into gear a year ago and thought that they were done. Even further behind now.

I’ve never seen a technology in my life and career that improves at this rate, which consequently means you need to upgrade your expectations at a similar rate. Our brains weren’t wired for this, and our organizational change management processes certainly weren’t either.

With any form of recursive self improvement, things just get wilder. It’s a time when you will need to be constantly reevaluating the things that didn’t work just a couple months ago to see if they now can be solved. AI native companies certainly have a strong advantage due to this right now, so now it comes down to can the bigger companies keep up. Wild times.

我们需要重构并重写大部分软件，以适应一种全新的、更快的节奏。

以往代码是一滴一滴汇聚而来的。很快，甚至可以说现在，代码的编写就会像一条连续的水流，宛如一条汹涌的河流随心所欲地蜿蜒奔腾。

这并不是什么新鲜事：大型科技公司过去凭借庞大规模的工程团队来应对这一点。但现在 AI 为每位工程师都配备了一支极具弹性且能力超群的劳动力。现在轮到你来面对这个问题了，
items.original:
we will need to rebuild and rewrite much of software to adapt to a new, faster pace. 

code used to arrive one drop at a time. soon, if not already, code will be written as if it were a continuous stream, like a violent river twisting and turning as it pleases. 

this is not a new thing: big tech cos have had to deal with this with the enormous scale of their engineering teams. but now ai has brought an incredibly elastic and capable workforce wielded by every engineer. this is your problem now, and the only way to adapt is to evolve your systems so agents - even and especially the ones with little context about the right way of doing things - can thrive. make the easy thing the right thing. 

your codebase is becoming organic architecture. agent contributions grow around the constraints and guardrails you’ve designed. good software engineering matters even more now! and no, the continuous stream of code is not something you have to watch helplessly. be more ambitious and design systems, frameworks, and languages to control the chaos. 

the time for mourning coding is long over

items.original:
🚨🚨🚨 Americans, you carry a historic responsibility. 🚨🚨🚨

Not only toward yourselves. Toward the entire world.

Let me explain why.

I'm French. I run an AI company. I live between Paris and San Francisco, so I see both sides of the Atlantic. And I can see what's coming.

We are living through the most consequential civilizational shift in human history. AI is not another tech cycle. Within ten years it will rewrite how we work, how we learn, how we create wealth, and how we decide what is true.

AI can become the greatest instrument of freedom ever built, or the most perfect instrument of control. Same technology. The only difference is who writes the rules.

That is the choice in front of you.

On one side, the world the globalists have been dreaming of for decades. A managed society run by unelected institutions, from Brussels to Davos. Experts deciding what you may say, what you may buy, what counts as true. And now, with AI, the tools to enforce it at scale.

On the other side, a new world, far fairer. Built on reality instead of narratives. Where you can build, speak and trade without asking permission. Where we finally stop building entire systems on lies everyone can see.

If the Democrats take back power, there's a strong chance the first world wins.

How can I be so sure? Because I live in the trailer.

In Europe, the machinery is already built.

The Digital Services Act lets Brussels fine a platform up to 6% of its global revenue for failing to manage "systemic risks" as vague as "negative effects on civic discourse." The first fine ever issued under it went to X. €120 million.

The digital euro: in July, the European Parliament voted 416 to 169 to move it forward. It is now being finalized in closed-door negotiations, with a deal targeted before the end of the year and a launch aimed at 2029. A central bank currency where your financial privacy depends on rules politicians can rewrite later.

Speech under supervision. Money under supervision. Now add an AI that can read everything, everywhere, in real time.

You think it stays in Europe? The DSA already applies to your platforms. And your protection against a digital dollar today? An executive order the next president can erase with one signature, and a ban that passed the House and is still stuck in the Senate.

The Senate. Again.

You have something we don't have in Europe. A man who cannot be bought, because there is nothing left that anyone could offer him. Elon Musk.

Love him or hate him, you know he's authentic. He bought Twitter and gave you your voice back. He has been smeared, boycotted and targeted by every institution that used to own the narrative, and he never bent. He never made a deal with the devil.

When a man like that tells you everything comes down to 51 senators, you listen.

Read his post again. Two new states: four new senators. A bigger Supreme Court: a new majority overnight. Mass legalization: a new electorate. Change the rules of the game once, and you never have to win it again.

That is not a policy agenda. That is an exit from democracy. And once the door is locked from the inside, the European machine crosses the Atlantic. The speech police. The supervised money. The managed truth. All of it running on AI.

Europe was the trailer. Don't let America become the movie.

The entire West is watching you. If America falls, there is nowhere left to go. You are the last country on Earth where an ordinary citizen can still say no, and make it count.

On November 3rd, vote like the free world depends on it.

This time, it does.

items.original:
Saw a few discussions about size of hack, why impact to bitcoin price is small, etc. 👇 

$6.3 billion is the biggest in USD terms, but not in BTC terms. MtGox was 650,000 BTC!

Other important numbers to consider:

% of bitcoin (in relation to BTC total supply), ie, market impact. MtGox is big there again at 5%+.

Number of users impacted, and % of user assets impacted. MtGox (the largest CEX at the time) and FTX (not small) were all near 100% of users and their asseets.

Most important: Who is impacted? Does the platform cover it all? (only one victim), as in recent two CEX cases and Binance.

Obviously, still a major disaster for the industry, Binance (and me). It hurts, but we survive. 

Most importantly, we protect our users.

(image from @MatthewRoszak)

The Binance hacker might have just pulled off one of the smartest moves I’ve seen in crypto.

First, Tether froze $1.5 billion in USDT.

Then Circle froze another $800 million in USDC.

At that point, it looked like the hacker’s money was trapped.

But apparently, he had already planned for that.

Instead of holding the stolen USDT in a wallet, he allegedly deposited it into Aave and used it as collateral to borrow ETH.

Then he walked away.

That’s where the story gets crazy.

Tether can freeze the USDT sitting in the wallet.

But it can’t freeze the ETH he already borrowed.

So now Aave is left holding frozen collateral, while the hacker is sitting on liquid ETH.

And unless the protocol can recover it somehow, he may not even need to pay the loan back.

Two companies froze billions of dollars in seconds.

But someone who understood how to use DeFi may have found a way around both of them.

Pretty insane when you think about it.

items.original:
La investigación inicial de Binance sugiere que el incidente de seguridad podría estar relacionado con la laptop comprometida de un ingeniero de DevOps, lo que le permitió a un atacante acceder a un contenedor de servicio y enviar transacciones de retiro no autorizadas. No encontramos evidencia de ninguna filtración de claves privadas de billeteras. Compartiremos un informe técnico detallado posterior al incidente una vez que la investigación haya finalizado y los hechos se hayan verificado por completo.

El impacto total estimado asciende a aproximadamente 6,300,000,000 USD. Trabajamos con socios de blockchain para congelar los activos afectados y, hasta el momento, se congelaron aproximadamente 3,000,000,000 USD en la cadena.

Binance cubrirá todas las pérdidas con los fondos de SAFU y de la empresa. Los fondos de los usuarios están a salvo. También publicaremos una Prueba de Reservas actualizada una vez que completemos las medidas correctivas.

Como medida de precaución inmediata, Binance:

suspendió temporalmente los depósitos y retiros mientras se completan los controles de seguridad;

revocó la autorización de la dirección afectada;

contactó a las autoridades y a socios de inteligencia de blockchain para rastrear y recuperar los fondos.

Nuestros equipos trabajan sin descanso para resolver este problema de forma segura y exhaustiva. Trabajamos estrechamente con las autoridades para confirmar la identidad de estos delincuentes y llevarlos ante la Justicia.

Confiá únicamente en los canales oficiales de Binance para recibir novedades. Si tenés más preguntas, no dudes en comunicarte con Atención al cliente de Binance.

¡Gracias por tu apoyo!

Equipo de Binance

如果我是你，我现在会强烈考虑卸载任何第三方 JS 脚本。特别是如果它来自初创公司的话。

分析、监控等都会带来巨大的网站接管风险。如果你使用来自第三方 SaaS 的跟踪脚本，那么一旦他们被黑，黑客就能完全控制你的网站。

这就是今天 Polymarket 瘫痪的原因。他们使用了一个来自跟踪页面加载速度的 SaaS 的微小脚本。那家公司被黑了，黑客随后从 Pol 窃取了数百万
items.original:
I would strongly consider uninstalling any third party js right now if I were you. Especially if it comes from a startup.

Analytics, monitoring, etc are all massive site takeover risks. If you use a tracking script from a third party SaaS, then if they get hacked the hackers have total control over your site too.

This is what took down Polymarket today. They used a tiny script from a SaaS that tracks page load speed. That company got hacked, and the hackers subsequently stole millions from Polymarket users.

If you want to use analytics safely, I would use a product that lets you pin the tracking script and control when it changes. Most of the mature products support this, e.g. Sentry, Amplitude, PostHog, Mixpanel, Heap. If not, you need to trust the company behind it a lot...

Railway got hacked last week. Railway! That's a very competent team, with particularly strong infra chops. The agent swarms are on another level.

A typical analytics company is nowhere near as sophisticated. You should ask yourself: do I trust this company's security more than Railway? I was an analytics CTO in a past life, and I will be the first to admit: we had some great people but we were not on this level.

We (Detail) just uninstalled our session replay, which was a product I loved but is not worth the risk right now.

I hate to write this because I spent a good chunk of my 20s benefitting from product teams taking a chance on a nothing startup and installing our js on their site. But in the past two weeks this risk vector has exploded. It's better for the ecosystem if we move away from third party js as fast as we can.

这绝非普通的代码吸血工具，而是专门针对币安14号架构定制开发的：

- 在归集ETH时精确保留恰好1个以太坊（`bal - 1 ether`），这样币安的自动化热钱包队列就不会因Gas不足报错而触发警报。
- 使用底层的 `staticcall` 加 `continue` 循环以及自定义错误代码（`SweepItemFailed`），以确保某一个报废或被列入黑名单的ERC-20代币不会导致整笔60亿美元的批量操作回滚。

items.original:
Reading the reconstructed bytecode of the Binance EIP-7702 sweeper (`0x63e8...6fae`) is wild.

This wasn't a generic drainer. It was custom-engineered for Binance 14's architecture:

- Leaves exactly 1 ether behind (`bal - 1 ether`) when sweeping ETH so Binance's automated hot wallet queue wouldn't error on gas and trip alarms.
- Uses raw `staticcall` + `continue` loops with custom error codes (`SweepItemFailed`) so one bricked or blacklisted ERC-20 wouldn't revert the $6B batch.
- Includes a custom `callExecute` function to impersonate Binance 14 as controller of an external vault holding $823M in USDC.

They leave a comment: "robberies could be prevented if getaway cars were slower."

You can't fully blame EIP-7702, but it sped up the attack. Without 7702, draining 64 tokens plus an external $823M vault from a live exchange hot wallet meant fighting moving nonces across 70+ transactions. Defense systems would've killed it after tx #3.

With 7702, Lazarus sprayed 50 consecutive nonces in one type-4 payload, turned an EOA into a custom proxy, and atomically swept billions in a single block.

Ethereum core devs built the ultimate getaway car. Surgical state-sponsored engineering.

This could be etched onchain:
`if (bal > 1 ether) { https://t.co/ou2j9VqGvv{value: bal - 1 ether}(""); }`

2. 执行阶段：攻击者提交包含 50 个预签名授权（nonce n 到 n+49）的 EIP-7702 批处理，以击中币安 14 号钱包波动的 nonce 窗口。

items.original:
The Binance $5.6B drain is a masterclass in modern EVM exploitation.

It wasn't a complex logic bug. It was an EIP-7702 delegation hijack:

1. Setup: Attacker funds 0x7c86 via Tornado Cash, deploys a sweep contract (0x63e8), and runs three live dry-runs on external wallets.
2. Execution: Attacker submits an EIP-7702 batch with 50 pre-signed authorizations (nonce n to n+49) to hit Binance 14's moving nonce window.
3. One authorization hits. Instantly, Binance 14 (an EOA) is reprogrammed to run the attacker's contract bytecode.
4. Execution looks totally organic: Binance 14 sweeps itself clean. Internal threshold alerts don't trigger because, from the nodes' perspective, the hot wallet is just executing its own transaction.
5. Binance 16 immediately auto-refills 28,000 ETH due to automated treasury rebalance scripts, feeding the exploit loop.

The cold truth: you cannot forge an EIP-7702 delegation list.
For this to execute, the attacker already held the raw private key or unconstrained signing access to Binance 14's HSM/KMS.

But hey, 5.64 billion drained across ETH, BTC, and Tron. 2.54 billion frozen by Tether, Circle, Ripple, and World Liberty within hours.

Code is law until the stablecoin admin keys log in.

Binance got bailed out by the very centralized choke points the cypherpunks warned you about.

Hardware wallets leak your home address.
Centralized exchanges leak the keys to the kingdom.

Self-custody on native, non-delegated chains remains the only honest baseline.

At least you know what to avoid.

أنت تشاهد الآن انهياراً حياً لقلب النظام المالي الرقمي العالمي. الجدران الأمنية لأكبر منصة تداول في العالم سقطت، وما كان يُعتقد أنه الخزنة الأكثر أماناً للعملات المشفرة، يُستنزف الآن بمليارات الدولارات في هجوم يهدد بابتلاع قطاع التمويل اللامركزي (DeFi) بأكمله.

الاختراق الأضخم في تاريخ العملات الرقمية: كيف سقطت جدران "باينانس"؟

في الساعات الأولى من يوم 30 أكتوبر 2026، ضرب زلزال مدمر أسواق العملات الرقمية مع تأكيد تعرض منصة "باينانس" (Binance) لاختراق كارثي. القراصنة لم يكتفوا بثغرة بسيطة، بل تمكنوا من تحويل أصول مسروقة تقدر قيمتها بما لا يقل عن 5.5 مليار دولار، مما يضعنا أمام واحدة من أضخم عمليات السطو الرقمي في التاريخ.

سباق التجميد وغسيل الأموال اللامركزي
بمجرد اكتشاف الكارثة، سارعت الكيانات الكبرى لمحاصرة المهاجم. قامت شركات إصدار العملات المستقرة، وعلى رأسها (Tether) و (Circle)، بتفعيل بروتوكولات الطوارئ وتجميد أكثر من 2 مليار دولار من عملات USDT و USDC المرتبطة بالاختراق. كما تدخل فريق شركة (Ripple) لتجميد حوالي 200 مليون دولار من عملة (RLUSD)، في حين صرحت إدارة "باينانس" أن أموال المستخدمين بأمان.

لكن المهاجم كان متقدماً بخطوة؛ فلتجنب فخ التجميد المبرمج في العقود الذكية للعملات المستقرة، بدأ القراصنة عمليات غسيل أموال واسعة النطاق عبر منصات التبادل اللامركزية (مثل Uniswap) لتحويل العملات المسروقة إلى عملة الإيثريوم (Ether)، مستغلين غياب سلطة مركزية قادرة على تجميد عناوين الإيثريوم.

خطر العدوى: الرعب الحقيقي يضرب الـ DeFi
الخطورة القصوى لهذا الاختراق لا تكمن فقط في السرقة المباشرة، بل في التكتيك الخبيث الذي استخدمه المهاجم لاختراق بروتوكولات الإقراض اللامركزي. بدلاً من مبادلة جميع العملات المستقرة وبيعها، قام المهاجم بإيداع 60 مليون دولار من عملة USDT كضمان (Collateral) في منصة (Aave)، ليقترض مقابلها 19,762 إيثريوم.

هذا التحرك الماكر يهدد بخلق "أزمة ائتمانية" (Credit Crunch) شاملة. فإذا تم تجميد العملات المستقرة المودعة كضمانات، ستعجز بروتوكولات الإقراض عن تسييلها (Liquidation) عند الحاجة، مما يعني انتقال عدوى الانهيار لكامل قطاع التمويل اللامركزي. وحذر الخبراء من أن هذه الخطوة تضع السيولة البديلة للعملات الرقمية (Altcoins) في خطر شديد.

إجراءات الطوارئ وانهيار الأسواق
أمام هذا الخطر الوجودي، انتفضت بروتوكولات الإقراض لحماية نفسها. فرضت منصة (Aave) قيوداً صارمة وحظرت الاقتراض والودائع الجديدة، بينما أوقفت منصة (Kamino) المبنية على شبكة سولانا (Solana) أسواق الإقراض المرتبطة بـ Solana و Bitcoin مؤقتاً كإجراء احترازي.

في هذه الأثناء، تعيش الأسواق حالة من التخبط الملحوظ؛ حيث تراجعت القيمة السوقية الإجمالية للعملات الرقمية بنسبة 5.72%، وارتفعت هيمنة البيتكوين (Bitcoin Dominance) كملاذ أخير. وتُشير التوقعات إلى مسار هبوطي سلبي على المدى القصير والمتوسط، فإذا لم يتم احتواء تداعيات الأصول المجمدة والضمانات المعلقة، فإن قطاع الكريبتو بأكمله يقف على أعتاب أزمة ثقة خانقة قد تطول لفترة غير معلومة.

items.title: 如果你对昨晚币安被黑之后比特币价格波澜不惊感到好奇，作为参考，2014 年门头沟（Mt Gox）被黑事件损失了约 75 万枚比特币，相当于当时大约 30 天的交易量。而昨天币安被黑事件损失了 18270 枚比特币，仅占如今比特币单日交易量的约五分之一，因此门头沟事件对价格的冲击严重了约 167 倍。
items.original: If you are wondering about the somewhat muted price impact to Bitcoin after last night's Binance hack, for reference, the MT Gox hack of 2014 was ~750K Bitcoin, which was about 30 days of trading volume at the time. Yesterday's Binance hack was 18,270 Bitcoin, or roughly 1/5th of a single day of Bitcoin's trading volume today, making Mt Gox ~167X worse for price impact.

随着抛售压力蔓延，纳斯达克100指数盘中已下跌近-5%。

在这次市场下挫期间，2天内就上升了+7个百分点。

我们尚未收到特朗普政府就当前市场状况做出的置评。

然而，显而易见的是，今天市场的走势时机……
items.original:
The timing of today's market crash is noteworthy.

As selling pressure spreads, the Nasdaq 100 is now down nearly -5% on the day.

Meanwhile, the market-implied odds of a Democrat "sweep" in the Midterms next week has surged from 65% to 72% today, a record high.

That's +7 percentage points in 2 days amid this market downturn.

We have yet to receive a comment from the Trump Administration regarding the current situation in the market.

However, what is clear is that the timing of today's market crash will be consequential.

And, even as technology stocks drop sharply, US Treasury Yields are barely seeing any relief.

This leaves us with high rates, a falling stock market, $100+ oil prices, and rising CPI, PPI, and PCE inflation.

Next week is going to be interesting, to say the least.

I am sorry to say, Madam Finance Minister, this is utter nonsense. 

Instead of lecturing us about the past, you must tell us what urgency led the government to sell such a major asset at 14% below the original reserve price at a time when:

1. India's stock market is one of the worst-performing of all 47 countries in the MSCI.
2. Foreign ownership of Indian equities is at an about a 15-year low.

Governo Lula firma contrato para preparar privatização dos Correios

Escritório receberá R$7,097 milhões para examinar a entrada de acionistas privados na estatal, enquanto a direção enfrenta greves e põe patrimônio à venda
PUBLICADO EM: 30/10/2026

Os Correios firmaram um contrato de R$7,097 milhões com o escritório Pinheiro Neto que inclui a preparação de sua transformação em sociedade de economia mista e de uma possível oferta de ações na Bolsa. A informação, publicada por O Globo em 23 de outubro, mostra a direção da estatal trabalhando para permitir a entrada de capital privado. Ainda não há decisão de vender ações, mas o governo já encomendou o serviço jurídico para examinar essa operação.

A lista de dezessete serviços inclui estudar a necessidade de autorização do Congresso, definir a estrutura societária, preparar o registro de companhia aberta, auxiliar potenciais compradores e redigir contratos de venda de ações. A contratação ocorreu sem licitação, segundo O Globo.

Numa sociedade de economia mista, a União pode manter a maioria das ações com direito a voto. Investidores privados receberiam parte dos resultados. É uma concessão aos capitalistas dentro de um serviço público construído com recursos nacionais. O plano examina ainda parcerias e venda de ativos: pedaços da estatal podem ser entregues sem tirar o nome do governo da porta. Trata-se de um eufemismo para privatização.

A direção invoca prejuízos de R$8,5 bilhões em 2025 e de cerca de R$5,5 bilhões no primeiro semestre de 2026. Em abril, contratou a consultoria McKinsey. Agora vieram os advogados. Também negocia R$7 bilhões em novos empréstimos com bancos, após contrair R$12 bilhões no fim de 2025. Para os trabalhadores dos Correios, a resposta à crise tem sido cortar direitos e postos de trabalho.

O ministro da Fazenda, o neoliberal Dario Durigan, já havia anunciado a escolha do governo. Em entrevista à GloboNews, em agosto, declarou: “Eu não tenho dilema em discutir segmentar atividades dos Correios, fazer com que você tenha mais joint ventures, ou seja, parcerias com a iniciativa privada”. Falou também em usar empréstimos para financiar investimentos, “alienação de ativos e parcerias com a iniciativa privada”. Primeiro o ministro propôs dividir as atividades da estatal com grupos particulares. Agora a direção paga para saber como abrir seu capital.

A alienação de patrimônio já foi tentada no Rio de Janeiro. A antiga sede nacional dos Correios, construída em 1878 na Rua Primeiro de Março, foi posta em leilão este ano por R$53,6 milhões. O edifício ocupa um quarteirão perto da Praça XV e faz parte de um conjunto histórico tombado. No leilão de 22 de outubro, porém, não houve ofertas: o prédio não foi vendido. Apesar disso, a decisão de pô-lo à disposição dos compradores permanece.

Em 2023, Lula retirou os Correios do Programa Nacional de Desestatização, no qual Bolsonaro havia incluído a estatal. Mas o decreto não impediu a empresa do governo de leiloar imóveis, procurar sócios privados e encomendar estudos para vender ações. Mesmo com o governo formalmente no comando, serviços e receitas podem ser transferidos a particulares.

Os ataques são anteriores a Bolsonaro. Aliás, eles são um método tradicional do próprio presidente Lula. Em 2008, no segundo mandato de Lula, um novo Plano de Cargos, Carreiras e Salários extinguiu o cargo de motorista e reuniu funções distintas sob a denominação de agente de Correios. A mudança facilitou a terceirização. Setores da direita permaneceram na direção da empresa, enquanto sindicalistas do PT e do PCdoB passaram à administração patronal.

Naquele mesmo ano, uma greve de carteiros alcançou mais de vinte estados. Os empregados cobravam o pagamento permanente de um adicional salarial. A direção dos Correios pediu ao Tribunal Superior do Trabalho que suspendesse a paralisação; como alternativa, exigiu que 70% do pessoal continuasse trabalhando, sob ameaça de multa de R$100 mil à Fentect. Os grevistas conquistaram o adicional de 30%, mas tiveram de compensar as horas paradas. Foi assim que o governo do antigo dirigente sindical tratou os funcionários que cruzaram os braços.

Em setembro de 2009, 27 dos 35 sindicatos da categoria recusaram uma proposta de acordo que valeria por dois anos e mantiveram a greve. A estatal voltou a recorrer ao TST. Lula criticou publicamente as lideranças do movimento e advertiu os empregados de que poderiam perder salário com o desconto dos dias parados. Sua administração tentava conter a mobilização justamente quando os trabalhadores exigiam reajuste, contratações e melhores condições de serviço.

A ofensiva não terminou com os mandatos anteriores. Em dezembro de 2025, já sob o atual governo Lula, uma greve por salários e direitos levou novamente os Correios ao TST. O tribunal determinou que 80% dos empregados permanecessem em serviço em cada unidade e fixou multa diária de R$100 mil aos sindicatos. Em janeiro de 2026, a direção da empresa obteve no STF a suspensão do abono de fim de ano, da gratificação de férias e de outras cláusulas trabalhistas. Em setembro, diante de outra greve contra mudanças no plano de saúde, a empresa recorreu mais uma vez à Justiça, que impôs a manutenção de 80% do efetivo.

Os Correios alcançam localidades onde uma transportadora privada não manteria atendimento regular por falta de lucro. Essa rede pode distribuir livros, medicamentos e mercadorias, integrar o território e apoiar o desenvolvimento nacional. Precisa de investimentos, concursos e recuperação dos serviços entregues a terceiros.

Durigan já indicou o que se pode esperar do novo governo Lula: mais participação privada, venda de patrimônio e contenção de despesas imposta à empresa. Vai trabalhar pela privatização total dos Correios. Aos empregados que resistem, a direção responde com pedidos ao TST.

Os trabalhadores dos Correios precisam organizar suas bases, unir os sindicatos e enfrentar cada retirada de direito e cada passo de privatização. A luta deve exigir a reestatização completa da empresa, sob controle dos trabalhadores, e a ampliação dos serviços públicos dos Correios em todo o País.

【震撼】世界第一投资家巴菲特称“股市已沦为赌场”的发话实在太顶了 笑

投资者：“每天买卖股票更赚钱吗？”
巴菲特：“你觉得那样谁最赚钱？”

投资者：“难道不是我们吗？”
巴菲特：“是华尔街。”

投资者：“哈？”
巴菲特：“你每次交易他们都能赚到钱。”

投资者：“……？”
巴菲特：“比如说，如果持有优质公司的股票50年呢？”

投资者：“那也太无聊了吧 笑”
巴菲特：“对华尔街来说将是最糟糕的。”

投资者：“为什么？”
巴菲特：“因为赚不到佣金手续费了。”

投资者：“确实……”
巴菲特：“如果在1965年买了伯克希尔股票，大家都一直持有呢？”

投资者：“……”
巴菲特：“华尔街恐怕早就饿死了吧 笑”

投资者：“那我每天看K线图岂不是……”
巴菲特：“可能就跟在拉老虎机的摇杆差不多吧。”

I'm dumping the majority of my Intel shares. This was genuinely one of the saddest earnings calls.

I had SO much hope for this company. I genuinely believed Intel was finally turning things around under Lip-Bu Tan and to be fair, they've made some real progress. But after listening to the entire earnings call, I honestly think Intel messed up BAD. And what makes this even more frustrating is that Intel has one of the biggest opportunities in the semiconductor industry sitting right in front of it, yet it cannot fully take advantage of it.

First, the guidance was absolutely terrible. Intel reported $16.5 billion in Q3 revenue and adjusted EPS of $0.52, which were actually pretty solid results. But then management guided for just $15 billion to $16 billion in Q4 revenue, compared to Wall Street's expectations of around $17.1 billion. They also expect adjusted EPS to fall to $0.25, compared to expectations of roughly $0.43. Even worse, gross margins are expected to fall from 44.1% to just 38% in a single quarter. That's a massive decline, especially for a company that's supposed to be improving its profitability.

But the biggest problem is what management said about 2027. Intel's PC business is getting destroyed by the ongoing memory shortage. Companies like Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron are benefiting from enormous AI demand, but that same demand is making memory more expensive and harder to find for traditional computers.

And when memory becomes more expensive, the entire computer becomes more expensive. That means fewer people and businesses are willing to upgrade their PCs, which directly hurts Intel. Management now expects the overall PC market to shrink by around 12% in 2026 and another 10% in 2027. Intel also expects its own client revenue to fall more than 20% in Q4 alone. What really caught my attention was when management basically admitted that they don't expect the memory situation to improve in 2027. So this isn't just a temporary problem that disappears next quarter. It could continue hurting Intel for another year or longer.

Now, here's what frustrates me the MOST. Intel's data center business is absolutely booming, but they cannot manufacture enough chips to meet demand. Data Center and AI revenue grew nearly 80% year over year to $7.3 billion. Management expects industry server CPU shipments to grow more than 30% in both 2026 and 2027, and Lip-Bu Tan even believes the server CPU market could grow from around $40 billion today to more than $200 billion over the next five years because of AI agents. That's an unbelievable opportunity. But Intel is dealing with manufacturing capacity limitations, production bottlenecks, and shortages of the materials needed to package its chips. In other words, customers WANT to buy more Intel server CPUs, but Intel cannot produce enough of them.

And management made it pretty clear that these supply problems will continue into the first half of 2027, with meaningful improvements not expected until the second half. This is what bothers me more than anything. We're experiencing one of the strongest periods of CPU demand in years, and Intel is leaving billions of dollars in potential sales on the table while competitors fight for market share. Then there's the tragic accident at Intel's factory in Israel, which forced production to shut down for approximately two weeks. Management expects this to reduce Q4 revenue by around $300 million, with a similar impact potentially extending into Q1. It also accounts for about two percentage points of the expected Q4 gross margin decline. Obviously, this was an unfortunate situation, but it creates even more problems for a company that was already struggling to produce enough chips.

And don't even get me started on the foundry business. This was supposed to be one of the biggest reasons to invest in Intel. The idea was that Intel could become a serious competitor to TSMC by manufacturing chips for other companies. And yes, Intel is making progress. Its 18A manufacturing process is improving, production costs are coming down, and management sounds more confident about 14A but here's the reality. Intel's foundry business still lost $1.9 BILLION in Q3. External foundry revenue was only $411 million, and part of that came from a one time customer program. Management keeps talking about potential customers, improving yields, and future opportunities. But where are the major external customer commitments that will actually make this business profitable? I'm not saying they won't come. I'm saying investors have already been waiting years for this turnaround, and we're still talking about what MIGHT happen in 2027 and 2028.

And then came another comment that really disappointed me. Intel doesn't expect to generate positive free cash flow in 2027. The company already expects to spend around $20 billion on capital expenditures in 2026, and management said spending will increase significantly next year. So we're looking at another year of massive investments, continued foundry losses, a declining PC market, and potentially negative free cash flow. And remember, Intel raised $23 billion by issuing additional shares in August, meaning existing shareholders also have to deal with dilution. At some point, investors need to ask when all this spending is actually going to translate into sustainable profits.

Now, I want to be fair because there ARE positives here. Intel's server CPU demand is incredibly strong. Its manufacturing technology is improving. Granite Rapids is becoming more profitable, its custom silicon business is growing rapidly, and its upcoming products like Diamond Rapids and Nova Lake could help it regain market share. I also think the long term opportunity in AI infrastructure, advanced packaging, and foundry services is enormous. But here's the issue. Almost every major positive Intel talks about is something that could happen in the FUTURE. More manufacturing capacity in the second half of 2027. Potential foundry customers. A stronger product roadmap. Better profitability. Eventually positive free cash flow.

Meanwhile, all the problems are happening RIGHT NOW. The PC business is declining right now. Manufacturing constraints are hurting sales right now. Foundry is losing billions right now. And margins are expected to fall significantly next quarter. The worst part is that Intel doesn't even have a demand problem in its server business. It has an execution problem. And that's arguably even more frustrating because the opportunity is already there.

I understand that rebuilding a company like Intel takes years, and I still respect what Lip-Bu Tan is trying to accomplish. But after the massive rally in this stock, investors were expecting Intel to finally start delivering meaningful results, not another year of excuses and promises. I was willing to be patient with Intel because I believed the turnaround was gaining momentum. But this earnings call genuinely changed my perspective.

I'm not selling because I suddenly believe Intel is a terrible company or that its technology has no future. I'm selling because I no longer think the risk and reward are nearly as attractive as they were before. I'm dumping the majority of my position, but I'll likely keep a smaller stake because I still believe there's long-term potential here. I really wanted Intel to succeed. I still do. But wanting a company to succeed and believing its stock is a good investment at the current valuation are two completely different things.

And after listening to management today, I just cannot justify maintaining the same level of exposure. Intel had the opportunity to prove that its turnaround was finally working. Instead, management gave investors even more reasons to question it. This was genuinely disappointing.

the irony of all of this is big tech is increasing their capex spend

but the capex beneficiaries (semis) aren’t being rewarded like they were earlier in the year

at the same time, big tech has to dillute and take on debt to afford to even spend the capex, which is causing issues in the credit market

and then you have the iran war which doesn’t help with oil

ultimately, I think there needs to be more evidence of a catalyst to create a structural sustained selloff given earnings/growth/labor market doesn’t support it, but it feels very obvious that the credit markets don’t want to support all this AI buildout 

and everything feels like a falling knife so few people are willing to step in and buy until there is meaningful technical recovery 

which is getting discounted into the semi’s valuations AND the hyperscalers

so the question is…what’s the better buy?

to me, it is obviously the hyperscalers on sustainability of earnings/growth but with more debt and dilution, their stocks have the risk of continuing to stay flat until fcf comes back to being positive 

gold and bitcoin also are participating as risk is being taken off across the board 

and then the fed raising rates makes it even harder for neoclouds to justify their ability to take on debt

long term, i think there are many names that are fundamentally undervalued given their growth and prospects but sentiment across the entire market, even after record big tech earnings, is just not good

💰️️️️️️✉️ Governo Lula firma contrato para preparar privatização dos Correios

Os Correios firmaram um contrato de R$7,097 milhões com o escritório Pinheiro Neto que inclui a preparação de sua transformação em sociedade de economia mista e de uma possível oferta de ações na Bolsa. A informação, publicada por O Globo em 23 de outubro, mostra a direção da estatal trabalhando para permitir a entrada de capital privado. Ainda não há decisão de vender ações, mas o governo já encomendou o serviço jurídico para examinar essa operação.

A lista de dezessete serviços inclui estudar a necessidade de autorização do Congresso, definir a estrutura societária, preparar o registro de companhia aberta, auxiliar potenciais compradores e redigir contratos de venda de ações. A contratação ocorreu sem licitação, segundo O Globo.

Numa sociedade de economia mista, a União pode manter a maioria das ações com direito a voto. Investidores privados receberiam parte dos resultados. É uma concessão aos capitalistas dentro de um serviço público construído com recursos nacionais. O plano examina ainda parcerias e venda de ativos: pedaços da estatal podem ser entregues sem tirar o nome do governo da porta. Trata-se de um eufemismo para privatização.

Bud Light was America’s #1 beer for over 20 years.Peak volume: ~41 million barrels.

Still the undisputed king heading into 2023.

Then the first woman ever to run its marketing, Alissa Heinerscheid, took over in 2022. She said the brand was “fratty” and “out of touch,” and needed to “evolve and elevate” with more inclusivity to attract younger drinkers.

April 2023: partnership with Dylan Mulvaney.

Result: lost the #1 spot, volumes cratered, and it’s still bleeding years later (projected ~12.7 million barrels in 2026 — down roughly 70% from peak).

She wanted a new era. She got one. Just not the one she had in mind.

items.original:
Kalshi just raised an additional $1B, valuing the company at $40B. This will help us expand into stocks, compute, indices, and institutional.

Tomorrow marks 8 years since we got accepted into YC and the journey began.

The odds of a kid from Lebanon getting here were pretty low.

Growing up there was great, but very challenging. We went through war. We had bombs explode in front of my house. I watched brilliant people’s lives destroyed for reasons beyond their control.

Lebanon is an unpredictable country. That unpredictability made it hard to plan for success. And yet despite it all, my mom sacrificed everything to give me and my brother the chance to go back to the US.

I found my refuge in two things: anime and math. Especially math.

I loved math because it calmed me. It was the opposite of unpredictable: clear, deterministic, orderly, and consistent. The proof is either right or wrong. I find that elegant and beautiful.

I was lucky.

I made it to my dream school, MIT (largely thanks to my mom), and my love for math quickly translated to a love for statistics, probability, and markets.

I love markets for a lot of the same reasons. Their incentives are clear: you get rewarded for being right and for pursuing knowledge. They are effective weighting machines for people’s opinions. They provide an incentive to be truthful, because they separate good information from bad information. They let people challenge the consensus and be rewarded for being right.

IMO, Hayek, Surowiecki, Hanson, Tetlock were the founding fathers of prediction markets. The more I read them, the more obsessed I got with the idea of applying market-based pricing to more things.

Markets bring rigor and critical thinking to more questions. And in an increasingly polarized and information-positioned word, I believe we need that more than ever.

Markets would also let people predict and manage more things outside of their control. And the world was becoming increasingly more unpredictable, and more like Lebanon, not less.

That love for markets got Luana and me to build Kalshi.

At first, it was mostly an idea we couldn’t stop talking about. We didn’t have much money. Luana’s sister bought the Kalshi domain name for us (for ~$1.7k). We moved to SF to get started, and embarked on a long, uncertain journey to build a regulated exchange.

The paranoia and anxiety from my childhood never left me. Even when things are going well, I think about what could go wrong. When people trust you with their money, that instinct serves a purpose.

I wanted us to build something that would hold up under pressure.

The first principle we defined at the company: regulatory-first. We worked with regulators for years before we listed a single market. We took every step to do things the right way and always asked for approval before proceeding. It was very hard at times, especially when we were being overtaken by competitors, but we believe doing things the right way matters.

Luana and I aren’t the only ones.

Our team put years of their lives into something far from certain. That’s especially true of Lior, Brandon, Rainer, Luis, Xavier, and Josef, who stuck with us for years. They believed when there was little to point to. And they stuck with us no matter how long it took. Kalshi is the result of an arduous journey through a long desert where, at times, most people didn’t understand why we were making the walk.

Many people still don’t understand what we’re doing and some disagree with us. Markets have historically taken time to be understood and accepted by some. But while not always obvious, their benefits are vast: capital markets help allocate capital and derivative markets help predict and manage uncertainty.

I firmly believe in these benefits, and that’s why I am dedicating my life to building this market.

Markets have caused issues many times in the past, and they certainly can present harms (manipulation, insiders, and addictive behaviors). These harms are more acute for certain types of markets (sports, short-term options, etc.) than others. It’s why I believe that guardrails need to exist and why we have taken the approach we have taken. We have consistently prioritized thinking critically about the risks and building the appropriate safeguards, sometimes beyond what the regulators require us to do. Many believe more needs to be done, and that’s a conversation I welcome.

Over time, I believe more people will see what we see: markets can help us get smarter and manage the future with more rigor, more precision, and more certainty than we have today.

To our tens of millions of users: you have made Kalshi bigger than anything Luana and I could have possibly imagined. Thank you for trusting us and thank you for coming along on the journey. I feel a strong responsibility to build a company worthy of that trust.

I am so lucky to spend my life building something I love. I hope everyone finds something they care about that much. Something that keeps you curious. Something that pushes you to your limits. Something that may put you at odds with the status quo. Something worth the hard days.

For me, it’s still markets. The more I learn, the more I want to understand.

我是村泽瑠依。
近日，我正式出任致力于构建太空电力基础设施的 Zero Industries 的“社区经理”（Community Manager）。

Zero 在创立仅仅半年内，就从包括前泽基金在内的投资者处筹集了约4.7亿日元。
公司正在研发利用激光将太空所发电力输送至人造卫星的技术机制，未来更以向太空数据中心及月球基地供电为目标。

领衔团队的，是年龄分别为16岁、19岁和20岁的创业成员：

从小学起便开始创业、曾参与7家公司创立与运营的 CEO 杉原海（16岁）。
高中时期发现并证明数学新定理、在全日本高中生统一测试决赛中斩获综合第一名的东京大学在读 CTO 藤井佑成（19岁）。
高中时创立一般社团法人并投身教育活动，如今掌管 Zero 经营根基的庆应义塾大学在读 COO 谷昊埜（20岁）。

我希望在连接人与人的岗位上，将自己的力量与他们的挑战相融合。
将他们创造的技术与描绘的未来传递给社会，连接起并肩作战的伙伴和支持者，让其潜能最大化。

以 Zero 为核心，搭建一个让全球年轻创业者以及在各领域开拓未来的先锋们相聚交流的平台
items.original:
【ご報告】
村澤瑠依です。
この度、宇宙の電力インフラ構築に挑むZero Industriesの「Community Manager」に就任しました。

Zeroは、設立から半年で、前澤ファンドをはじめとする投資家から約4.7億円を調達。
宇宙で発電した電力をレーザーで人工衛星に届ける仕組みを開発し、将来は宇宙データセンターや月面拠点への電力供給を目指しています。

率いるのは、16歳・19歳・20歳の創業メンバー。

小学生の頃から事業を始め、7社の創業・運営に携わってきたCEO・杉原海（16）。
高校時代に数学の新定理を発見・証明し、全国統一高校生テスト決勝で総合1位となった、東大生のCTO・藤井佑成（19）。
高校時代に一般社団法人を立ち上げ、教育活動にも携わり、現在はZeroの経営基盤を担う、慶應生のCOO・谷昊埜（20）。

僕は、彼らの挑戦に、人と人をつなぐ立場から自分の力を掛け合わせたい。
彼らが生み出す技術と、描く未来を社会へ届け、共に挑む仲間や支援者をつなぎ、その可能性を最大化する。

Zeroを軸に、世界の若い起業家や、各分野で未来を切り拓く人たちが出会う場をつくり、新しい挑戦につなげる。

全てを注ぐ覚悟で、挑みます。

Rui Murasawa / 
Community Manager of Zero Industries

我离开《大西洋月刊》时筹集了0美元，因为我觉得在为另一家杂志工作的同时筹款是不合适的。其他人做出了不同的选择，但这曾是我的选择。

由 Tyler Cowen 运作的 Emergent Ventures 旨在赋能那些认为自己能做大事的年轻人。Tyler 从该基金中给了我10万美元的资助来创立 @TheArgumentMag。

随后，我从拥有各种背景和兴趣的一众投资者那里筹集了400万美元，以打造一家自由主义杂志，
items.original:
I quit The Atlantic having raised 0 dollars because I felt it was inappropriate to raise money while working for another magazine -- others have made different choices but that was mine. 

Emergent Ventures, which is run by Tyler Cowen, exists to empower young people who think they can do big things. Tyler gave me a grant of $100,000 from this fund to build @TheArgumentMag. 

I then raised $4 million from an array of investors with various backgrounds and interests to build a liberal magazine where people could debate big questions. 

Zach, who has recieved direct or indirect funding from the founder of eBay, Charles Koch, Exxonmobil, Chevron, BP, JP Morgan Chase, AWS, Meta, and Google, is, I suppose, telling on himself about the nature and origin of his views.

Personally, I think Zach came by his flawed viewpoint honestly but if you follow his logic he's an agent of Big Oil and Big Tech. 

I find it galling when those who have been funded by tech billionaires and the failsons of the wealthy have the temerity to cast stones at anyone else for trying to make something of themselves despite not having access to institutional wealth. 

Perhaps if I had been born the daughter of a billionaire and devoted myself to the cause of making the left historically unpopular, I would have Zach's respect. Alas, I think I'll live without it.

items.title:
致10岁的我：

今年夏天，你将会邂逅一部名为《少年时代》（Juvenile）的电影。
然后，你会非常珍惜在电影院买的滚轮印章上面附带的那个小小Tetra机器宠。

十几年后，你得知株式会社ROBOT的社长室前摆着一只Tetra，于是制定了偷窃计划，去参加了面试，并成功入职。

然而，计划以失败告终。
顺便说一句，你现在还没离职。

而在电影上映26年后，Tetra的手办终于发售了。

虽然是80%比例，但你会买两只。
我现在正打算拆解其中一只，进行扫描，并利用3D打印机制作出一个1/1等比例的Tetra。

如果想要Tetra的话，长大之前就多多学习吧。
这可是F.I.D.啊。
items.original:
10歳のぼくへ。

君はこの夏、『ジュブナイル』という映画に出会う。
そして、劇場で買ったコロコロスタンプの上についてる小さなテトラを大切にするだろう。

その十数年後、株式会社ロボットの社長室の前にテトラがあることを知り、盗む計画を立て、面接に行き、見事入社する。

しかし、計画は失敗に終わる。
ちなみに、会社はまだ辞めていない。

そして映画から26年後、ついにテトラのフィギュアが発売される。

80%スケールだが、君は2つ買う。
僕はこれから1つをバラし、スキャンし、3Dプリンタを駆使して、1/1スケールのテトラを作る計画を立てている。

テトラが欲しかったら大人になるまでにたくさん勉強せよ。
F.I.D.だ。

“从1到10打分的话？手指在世界杯上给我的限制是10。直到对阵阿尔及利亚的前一天，我还只能单臂扑救，像个僵尸一样。

手一撑地就疼得眼冒金星，下巴受的这点伤跟那相比根本不算什么。我疼得哭到半夜12点，因为手指肿得像根血肠。

如果有哪个球砸在指尖上，我的整根手指都会炸裂。在每一次……”

“¿Del 1 al 10? El dedo me condicionó 10 en el Mundial. HASTA EL DÍA ANTES DE ARGELIA ME TIRABA CON UN BRAZO, COMO UN ZOMBIE.

Apoyaba la mano y era ver las estrellas, esto de la mandíbula no es nada al lado de eso. LLORABA HASTA LAS 12 DE LA NOCHE PORQUE TENÍA EL DEDO COMO UNA MORCILLA.

Si alguna pelota me hubiera pegado más en la punta me explotaba el dedo completo. En cada pelota que venía yo pedía que no se me zafe el dedo.

Gritaba del dolor cuando tenía que meter el dedo en el guante, pedía por favor que me corten el guante. Me duchaba con una bolsa y la mano arriba”.

items.original:
أنا يارا العمري، جدي شارك في توحيد المملكة مع الملك عبدالعزيز، وأبوي درع من دروع هذا الوطن، وله مواجهات مباشرة مع الإرهاب والحوثيين وداعش وخونة الوطن وغيرهم.

وأنا طالبة قانون ولاعبة في المنتخب السعودي، وأسخّر حاضري ومستقبلي وروحي لخدمة وطني، وهذا حسابي الرسمي، وأتحمّل مسؤولية كل كلمة أقولها.

وأقول لك إن التطبيل والاحتفاء والتمجيد لشخصٍ على أفعالٍ مثل أفعال عبدالله لا يمثّلني، ولا يمثّل كل مواطن شريف غيور على دينه ووطنه وولاة أمره.

ماني مع الشماتة، ولا أدعم بقاءه خارج الوطن، لكنّي أدعم محاسبته على ما ثبت في حقه، والإعتراف بأخطائه دون تبرير أو تهوين.

وأدعم قرارات الدولة بشأنه أيًّا كانت؛ لأنني أعيش في دولة حق وعدل، دولة تُدرك غيرة المواطن على دينه ووطنه ونسائه وولاة أمره، وتزن الأمور بميزان الشرع والنظام وما تراه مناسبًا لا بالعواطف والمجاملات.

لا نشمت، ولكن لا نبرّر أفعاله، ولا نمجّده وكأنه تفضّل علينا بعودته.

فالعودة إلى الوطن شيء، وتبرير الإساءة شيء آخر، والاحتفاء لا ينبغي أن يكون على حساب المبادئ.

Caleb Hammer has a “What in the world?” moment when he realizes his 34-year-old leftist guest is arguing that her town would be better off without jobs.

It started when she claimed billionaires and corporations don’t pay their “fair share.”

Then she brought up Amazon, and Hammer realized he was dealing with someone who is “f*cking BROKEN.”

LEFTIST: “But why are we giving tax returns to corporations?”

HAMMER: “Tax returns? What are you talking about, tax returns? You’re talking about where they spend more money than they make on paper, so they have to pay less taxes because they’re employing people, investing in R&D and new technology.

“They can pack up and move just like anyone else. They’ll go to Ireland for the corporate HQ. We don’t want that. You want to pull a UK where they all go to Dubai? No, thank you. I like when they’re here. There are consequences to performative policies.”

LEFTIST: “There are like Fortune 100 companies that have gotten tax money back from—”

HAMMER: “What kind of tax? What kind of tax?”

LEFTIST: “Chase Bank got a tax return. [...] I know like Amazon paid zero dollars in corporate—”

HAMMER: “Well, hold on. But that was because they spent more than they made for the longest time. They weren’t a profitable company until recent years. You know that, right? Are you saying companies should have to pay taxes on money when they’re not profitable?

“So, me as a business, let’s say we make a million dollars this year. If I spend a million 100,000, I should pay taxes on my lost money?”

LEFTIST: “No, if you’re—”

HAMMER: “Hold on. That was Amazon. That was also one of the biggest employers in, not with bad wages either, the entire country. You want to punish them?”

LEFTIST: “Not punish them, but I don’t think they should be getting—”

HAMMER: “What do you want to be, AOC, and prevent a brand new campus coming to New York with thousands of new jobs?”

LEFTIST: “There are like eight Amazon warehouses within driving distance of me. And they don’t do anything to better the community.”

HAMMER: “You know a lot of people work there, right? That’s benefiting your community. Those people put money into your system.”

LEFTIST: “That two-lane road [traffic] wouldn’t be a problem if Amazon wasn’t there.”

HAMMER: “This is actually impressive. I’ve never witnessed someone so far left that they’re actually advocating for degrowth policies. [...] They pay taxes, property taxes, which those warehouses certainly do. And income taxes and whatnot, paid to the state, redistributed to the city in the state of California thanks to their new jobs. It’s your city’s fault for not allocating the resources properly. Advocate for that.

“You went and advocated for a DEGROWTH POLICY. That’s one of the most insane things I’ve ever heard in my life.”

Something tells me this beatdown will replay in her head the next time she blames Amazon instead of the government for the roads.

Today, two visions of the world are colliding. And Bill Gates is probably the clearest example.

On one side, the people who build. On the other, the people who manage.

For 30 years, Gates has presented himself as the man who wants to save the world. But look closely at how it actually works.

His philanthropy is first and foremost a reputation machine. Millions poured into media, massive funding for supranational organizations, a presence everywhere the narrative gets written. When you fund the people who write the story, the story is rarely hard on you.

Then there's the model itself. Foundations, NGOs, grants. A system where money flows, reports pile up, conferences follow one after another, but the problem never actually needs to be solved. Because a solved problem is a cause that disappears. Grants keep the problem alive. Entrepreneurs kill it.

The Elon Musk episode sums it all up.

In 2022, Gates reaches out to Musk to talk about philanthropy and climate. Musk asks him one question: do you still have a half-billion-dollar short position against Tesla? Gates replies: sorry to say I haven't closed it out.

Read that again. The man who wants to save the planet from climate change was betting hundreds of millions on the collapse of the company that did more than anyone to electrify global transportation. And he was asking its founder to back his climate vision.

Musk said no. Obviously.

Because underneath, these are two irreconcilable philosophies.

Musk believes we need more. More energy, more humans, more planets. Abundance as the answer.

Gates believes we need to manage. Consume less, emit less, have fewer children. Ration, regulate, control. It's Malthus for the modern age: the conviction that humanity is a problem to contain rather than a force to unleash.

Bill Gates is the pure, sick product of our era. A society that rewards the appearance of goodness over goodness itself. That prefers the press release to the result. The charity gala to the factory.

And deep down, I find this man profoundly sad. To have had so much money, so much power, and to choose to manage the world instead of building it.

I have not drunk water in the last 48 years — Billionaire Warren Buffett 

Billionaire investor Warren Buffett has reportedly gone nearly five decades without drinking water, with his preferred beverage being Cherry Coke, according to fellow billionaire Bill Ackman. 

Ackman, founder and CEO of Pershing Square, shared the surprising revelation during an appearance on the Equity Mates Investing podcast. 

Recalling a dinner Buffett had at his home years ago, Ackman said he had stocked up on Cherry Coke, knowing it was the legendary investor’s favourite drink. 

While they were at the dining table, Ackman offered Buffett still or sparkling water, but the 96-year-old declined and requested his usual soda instead. 

Curious about his drinking habits, Ackman asked, “Don’t you drink water?” 

According to him, Buffett replied, “Bill, I haven’t had water in 48 years.” 

Buffett, who stepped down as Berkshire Hathaway’s CEO last December after six decades in the position and relinquished his chairmanship in September, is famously known for consuming about five cans of Coca-Cola daily. 

In 2015, he jokingly described himself as “one-quarter Coca-Cola,” explaining that the beverage accounted for roughly 25 per cent of his daily calorie intake. 

Beyond soda, Buffett is known for his preference for fast food and sugary treats, including McDonald’s, hot dogs, fries, popcorn, cookies, sweets and ice cream.

items.original:
Imagina vender tu casa para vivir en un crucero durante los próximos 15 años. Dos años después, el barco atraca en Camboya y la compañía le dice a todos que se bajen.

Eso acaba de sucederle a unas 200 personas. Y con los precios actuales del combustible, los $120,000 que pagaron por una cabina apenas cubren 15 meses de combustible.

El barco es el Villa Vie Odyssey. Fue construido en 1993, estuvo almacenado durante el Covid y una startup de Florida lo compró por unos $13 millones. Su propuesta era simple. Compras tu cabina por adelantado, empezando en unos $120,000, pagas una cuota mensual desde $1,750 por persona, y el barco navega alrededor del mundo sin parar durante 15 años.

Los problemas empezaron mucho antes de que algo saliera mal. La compañía dice que el combustible costaba unos $1,800 por cabina al mes antes de este año. Así que alguien que vivía solo en una cabina barata pagaba menos cada mes de lo que costaba solo el combustible para la cabina promedio, y eso sin contar alimentar a nadie, pagar a 156 tripulantes o reparar nada en un barco de 33 años.

Luego estalló la guerra de Irán en febrero y el combustible se disparó. En partes de Asia, la compañía dice que ahora cuesta entre $6,000 y $8,000 por cabina al mes.

Y se pone peor, porque un barco quema casi el mismo combustible ya sea que esté lleno o medio vacío. El Odyssey puede albergar a 650 pasajeros. Llegó a Camboya con 203 a bordo, así que el combustible para todas esas cabinas vacías lo estaban cubriendo las personas que realmente se presentaron.

Si estabas en el barco, probablemente podías sentir que se avecinaba. Un residente le dijo a la AP que les habían pedido dinero para combustible cada dos o cuatro semanas. 
Ahora la compañía dice que pasará 60 días trabajando en una "reestructuración y recapitalización". 
La mayoría de estas personas tenían prometidos 15 años en ese barco, y solo obtuvieron un poco más de dos.

Muchos pasajeros obtuvieron el dinero mediante préstamos. Bendito año 2026.

A strong decision by the U.S. State Department – authorizing Ukraine’s purchase of Patriot interceptors to counter Russian ballistic missiles. Five hundred PAC-3 interceptors is a substantial number, and very soon – this winter – they COULD make for a highly effective defense package. However, it has been stipulated that deliveries may begin ONLY IN A FEW YEARS. We are asking our American partners to find a solution for the time when there is a real danger and a real need to use PAC-3 interceptors.

Right now, the Russians are attacking our energy infrastructure every single day. In just these past two weeks of October, there have already been more than 30 Russian strikes on critical parts of our power grid. It is right now, even before the beginning of winter, that Putin has started carrying out his operation to attack the systems that sustain life in our cities and communities. The targets are electricity, heating, water supplies, bridges, and life in our cities in general.

We did ask our American partners to provide Ukraine with a winter support package – at a rate of 100 Patriot interceptors per month. Five hundred missiles would be enough to protect our skies over the coming months – precisely when it is so important for Ukraine to be in a strong position in negotiations and for Russia NOT to succeed in breaking life in Ukrainian cities and communities.

The United States, our European partners, and other partners around the world have sufficient stocks of PAC-3 interceptors in their warehouses. Providing them to Ukraine right now – in the winter of 2026–2027 – and replenishing our partners’ arsenals LATER, in THE FOLLOWING YEARS, through this production already contracted and paid for by Ukraine and our partners would be the right approach. And it is entirely feasible.

We are grateful to President Trump. Importantly, we recently discussed PAC-3 interceptors with Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Ukraine is grateful to the U.S. State Department and the U.S. Administration overall for granting this authorization. But we are asking for decisions that can guarantee the protection of lives not the day after tomorrow or sometime later, but at the very moment the threat is there – when Russia is killing and destroying. I thank everyone who stands with Ukraine!

ماذا لو نفذ ترامب تهديده بقصف إيران مره أخرى إيه اللي هيحصل؟

 المعطيات بتقول إن إيران مش ناوية تضرب الخليج المرة بالصواريخ بس..

 مسؤولين إيرانيين تحدثوا بتصريحات محكمة، إن عندهم خطط جاهزة لضرب كابلات الإنترنت البحرية في الخليج لو اتهاجموا تاني، ومنع إصلاحها عشان الانقطاع يطول..

يعني بعد الضربة الأولى أي محاولات لإصلاح الكابلات أو استعادة حركة البيانات هيتم قصفها..

 الحرس الثوري حدد 7 كابلات رئيسية تحت مضيق هرمز، ومحسن رضائي هدد بتدمير مراكز البيانات ومنشآت الذكاء الاصطناعي المرتبطة بأمريكا في منطقة الخليج بالكامل..

 يعني اللي صرف المليارات عشان يبقى عاصمة التكنولوجيا من سنوات ممكن يصحى يلاقي نفسه من غير إنترنت ولا بنوك ويرجع حرفيا لحياة القرن 19..

أحب افكرك إن في الحرب العالمية الأولى أغسطس 1914، بريطانيا ماضربتش ألمانيا بمدفع.. بل قطعت كابلات التلغراف بتاعتها تحت البحر، وعزلتها عن العالم في ساعات.. وده كان له تأثير سلبي على قوة ألمانيا في الحرب بالكامل.

 بعد أكتر من 100 سنة، إيران بتلعب نفس اللعبة..

واللي فاكر إن ده تهويل يتذكر يناير 2008، لما كابلات إنترنت اتقطعت في البحر المتوسط قدام إسكندرية، والإنترنت وقع في مصر والخليج والهند مرة واحدة.. ويفتكر 2024 لما 4 كابلات في البحر الأحمر اتضررت قصف الحوثيين لسفينة تابعة للكيان الصهيوني وغرقت، ومرساتها جرّت في القاع ولمست بعض الكابلات..

وقتها انخفضت قدرة الإنترنت في بعض الدول 25% تقريبا لعدة أيام عقبال ما صلحوها..

أما كابلات مضيق هرمز حضرتك ما بتتكلمش عن كابلات ممكن تتقطع بطريقة غير مقصودة وتتصلح، ولكن المرة دي متعمده وهتخضع لكل قوانين الحرب..

والسؤال دلوقتي: مين اللي هيدفع تمن الحرب دي فعلا..؟!.. هل دول المنطقه اصبحت عاجزه تماما لدرجه انها مش قادره توقف حرب ممكن تدمرها؟

It's almost hard to believe, but the US has only a single factory left that makes HMX and RDX, the explosives in nearly every modern missile and bomb - an aging wwii plant in Tennessee that's massively backordered.

A few years ago, a startup called Solugen was making chemicals for the petroleum industry, when by happenstance they heard about this problem.  It turns out that the same infrastructure they'd built for other chemicals was a perfect fit to make energetics.

So, that's what they're doing now.  They can already make 1/10 of what the old US army plant makes, and in the future will make much more.  

This is the SpaceX/Anduril moment for the US military explosives market.

items.original:
The Governor says 200,000 Washingtonians will lose Apple Health because of the federal bill.

Let's audit that.

What's the requirement?
80 hours a month of work, school, training, or volunteering.
Or about $580 a month in earnings.

Parents of kids under 14? Exempt.
Pregnant women? Exempt.

And for all of 2027, you can self-report.
No pay stubs. No proof. Just say it.

So why would 200,000 people lose coverage?

The state's own analysis says it: red tape.
Paperwork. Missed notices. Renewals that fall through the cracks.

Who runs the paperwork?
Olympia.

Now look at what Olympia chose to fund.

Apple Health for adults here illegally. 100% state dollars.
About $150 million, kept in the budget during a $16 billion deficit.

Gender transition care. If federal money stops, state money covers it.

Abortion. Covered with state dollars.

So when they say they can't protect working families' coverage, remember what they paid for first.

Not just a spending problem.
A priorities problem.

Audit before ask.

Source: WA Health Care Authority; WA State Standard
#VoicesUp #VoteTonya44 #RestoreWashington

Gister werd @MartinSellner_, activist founder van de @SaveEuropeAct, tegengehouden bij de Franse grens. Hij is vastgezet, moest een nacht in de cel doorbrengen en zal naar verwachting vandaag worden uitgezet.

Totaal ongekend. Terwijl honderdduizenden Afrikanen en Arabieren de grens met Frankrijk overlopen en migranten de hele binnenstad van oa Parijs afbreken, wordt een Oostenrijks staatsburger die naar een conferentie wilde de toegang tot het land wél ontzegd.

Dan kan het ineens wel. Dan zijn er ineens wel grenzen. Dan kan er wel worden gehandeld.

Ongelofelijk. Het laat zien hoe democratie en vrijheid van meningsuiting in het “vrije Westen” een illusie zijn geworden. 

Maar laat de boodschap duidelijk zijn: mensen kun je weren, ideeën niet. Remigratie gáát er komen. En juist door wat er nu met Martin gebeurt zullen mensen weer zien hoe nodig het is.
